request: Analyze GSE294565 for PMID 37872294 (Inhibition of p53-MDM2 binding reduces senescent cell abundance and improves the adaptive responses of skeletal muscle from aged mice.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

accessions: GSE294565 (GEO lists PMID 37872294; paper DA.p1 names BioProject PRJNA1029003)
final.assay: bulk mRNA-seq of tibialis anterior (TA), Novogene; plus NanoString GeoMx spatial RNA-seq (not in this GEO series)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of BI01 (OS) vs vehicle (OV) on the TA transcriptome of old mice 7 and 35 days after BaCl2 injury (S2.5.p1, FIG6). The only exercise-like stimulus in the paper, 28-day mechanical overload of plantaris by synergist ablation (S2.6.p1, S4.3.p1, FIG8-9), was assessed by histology and muscle mass only; no RNA-seq was done on overloaded muscle.
planned_contrasts: OS vs OV, 7 d post-BaCl2, n=4/group (S2.5.p1, FIG6a-b; paper: 'hundreds of genes', no count given)
OS vs OV, 35 d post-BaCl2, n=4/group (S2.5.p1, FIG6d-e; no count given)
final.sample_inclusion: 32 TA libraries: YV/OV PBS, YV/OV/OS 7 dpi and 35 dpi (no OS PBS libraries deposited)
final.repeated_measure_unit: PBS and BaCl2 were injected unilaterally (ABS.p1), but the library names give no animal ID, so contralateral pairing is not recorded
final.paper_method: Partek Flow: STAR to GRCm39, Partek E/M (Ensembl 103), min 10 counts filter, DESeq2 (S4.11.p1)
final.paper_results: DEG counts not stated; Tpt1 up in OS at 7 d, not different at 35 d (S2.5.p1, FIG6c,f)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.5.p1 and S4.11.p1 describe the only bulk RNA-seq: TA after BaCl2 injury, OV vs OS at 7 and 35 d (with YV reference). Mechanical overload (S2.6.p1, S4.3.p1) is the resistance-exercise model, but FIG8-9 report only muscle mass, fiber CSA and senescence staining; S4.11/S4.12 list no sequencing of plantaris. The paper's estimand for the deposited data is a drug effect after chemical injury, not exercise.

checks: GEO series lists Series_pubmed_id 37872294 (and 40259517) and reuses the paper's title and abstract
Series design (young/old TA, PBS vs BaCl2 7/35 dpi, BI01 cohort) matches S2.5.p1 and FIG6 (n=4/group)
Paper DA.p1 names BioProject PRJNA1029003 while the GEO series links PRJNA1250510 (recorded as a discrepancy; GEO was released Apr 2025, after the paper)
GEO data_processing says HISAT2/mm10 while the paper says STAR/GRCm39 Partek E/M (recorded as a discrepancy)

ownership.reasoning: The PMID link, title, abstract and exact group structure tie GSE294565 to this paper; the BioProject and aligner differences do not change which samples these are.

final.prep: prep_rename_columns.py renamed matrix lab codes to GSM ids; group codes map exactly (YV35dPBS->Young Vehicle PBS, OS27dBa->Old Senolytic 7 DPI, ...); within-group replicate pairing is ordinal and assumed (matrix replicate numbers 6-9/4-7/7-10 do not match GEO 1-4). Map: GSE294565_column_map.csv

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns are lab codes with replicate numbers that differ from GEO; no shared per-sample key exists. The group part of every code is unambiguous, so group labels are exact; which animal within a group is which is assumed ordinal. This would matter only for per-sample covariates or pairing, and the case stops at design before any model.

matrix.reasoning: Integer fraction 1.0, max 2.4e6, GEO data_processing 'tab-delimited count matrix' after HISAT2; paper used DESeq2 on Partek E/M counts (S4.11.p1).

design.stop_reason: No exercise contrast in the sequenced samples. GSE294565 holds only TA muscle after PBS or BaCl2 chemical injury (young/old, vehicle/BI01). The paper's exercise-like stimulus, 28-d synergist-ablation mechanical overload of plantaris (S2.6.p1, S4.3.p1), was not sequenced (FIG8-9 are histology/mass only). Injury-induced regeneration is not exercise, and BI01 vs vehicle is a drug effect, so no group comparison here answers how exercise affects gene expression.

candidates.value: grp O_S_D7 vs O_V_D7 and O_S_D35 vs O_V_D35 (paper's BI01 contrasts)
candidates.reason_rejected: drug effect after chemical injury, not an exercise effect
chemical myotoxic injury is not exercise or overload
no MOV or sham plantaris libraries in GSE294565 or anywhere stated in the paper

design.reasoning: Request asks for an exercise effect. The data identify injury, age and drug effects only; the paper never sequenced the overload model. Refused at design after recording paper, ownership, alignment and matrix.

discrepancies.disposition: recorded; ownership kept via PMID link and design match

discrepancies.paper: STAR v2.7.8a to GRCm39, Partek E/M Ensembl 103 (S4.11.p1)
discrepancies.disposition: recorded; not consequential because the case stops at design
